I don't rightly know why I did this, but I found some [data](http://b4tea.com/food-health/mcdonalds-nutrition-facts-food-chart-with-calories/), macro'd it into a set of data structures, and now I can sort, reduce and filter, as you do.

#S(food-item :name "Chipotle Barbeque Sauce" :serving-size 43 :calories 70 :calories-from-fat 0 :total-fat 0 :saturated-fat 0 :cholesterol 0 :sodium 260 :carbohydrates 16 :fiber 0 :sugars 14 :protein 0)

The only thing I was really curious about is the highest ratio of protein per calorie. The top five are variations on "salad with chicken". (And scrambled eggs.)

Caesar Salad with Grilled Chicken: 0.13333334 Bacon Ranch Salad with Grilled Chicken: 0.124

The dropoff is pretty sharp. Some of the interesting items:

Double Quarter Pounder with Cheese: 0.06438356 Chicken McNuggets: 0.05882353 McChicken: 0.035714287 Filet-O-Fish: 0.035

The Filet-O-Fish and McChicken are pretty close to the bottom, and perform about the same:

protein 14, calories 400

Compare that to the salad:

protein 28, calories 210

Get fucked, McChicken.

Selections from the bottom:

Hotcakes and Sausage: 0.019480519 Chocolate Chip Cookie: 0.0125 French Fries: 0.011538462 Salt Packet: 0.0

Side-by-side, you figure the fries must be made of sawdust, but here you have to refer to the complete data.

#S(food-item :name "Large French Fries" :serving-size 171 :calories 520 :calories-from-fat 220 :total-fat 25 :saturated-fat 5 :cholesterol 0 :sodium 330 :carbohydrates 70 :fiber 7 :sugars 0 :protein 6)

#S(food-item :name "Chocolate Chip Cookie" :serving-size 33 :calories 160 :calories-from-fat 60 :total-fat 7 :saturated-fat 2 :cholesterol 10 :sodium 95 :carbohydrates 22 :fiber 0 :sugars 14 :protein 2)

The salt packet contains 270 mg of sodium, and nothing else. I'm not sure if this is surprising to anyone.

Questions? Also, do you have more data for me to fuck around with?

The past few years have been rough for me. Financially (still not amazing in the sector) and mentally. I have been in the dumps for the better part of 5 years now. Not hard depression, just dissatisfied. Taoism and zen have helped me not worry about the small stuff that much, but the past few months have been fantastic and unlike anything else I have experienced.

I started working for a local restaurant (fine dining) that uses a lot of local and farm fresh foods. I had been out of the culinary industry for a few years because I hated it. It's hard work and not very rewarding - it also make having a family very difficult. So naturally I waited until I had a kid and jumped back into it. My brain is silly like that. This place has been amazing though, but my post isn't about my day to day work.

Earlier this week I got to cook at a very special place in New York City and showcase our local foods. I only helped, but my Chef was so grateful to have me there. It was such an honor. I want to say where we cooked for bragging rights, but it would make my identity easy to know. Either way, I'm just so fucking excited. I got to eat at amazing restaurants like Del Posto and Cosme when I was there and met all manor of wonderful people. One guy, a purveyor for our restaurant, roasts coffee as a hobby and is a mother-fucking rocket scientist by day. Literally. He also lives close and has a cool garden, we talked over a fancy dinner about coffee and growing food. He gave me his business card and told me to drop by.

I am just in awe. 2 months ago I was working a crappy office gig, now I am networking with my community that I felt so stranded from. I'm cooking and growing amazing food, and my boss/chef loves me. He knows cooking is only my second passion and wants to help me be more successful. He is even helping me network and find what job works best for me. So fucking cool, guys. I am so happy. I feel so much more Eudaimonia in my work than I have ever felt before.

If you're feeling stuck in life and have that nagging thought. If you're thinking about writing a novel, starting a garden, applying for a job you don't think you'll get, etc. Just fucking do it! Don't think, just jump right in. I finally have my momentum going and I feel like I'm going to make it somewhere great. I actually feel like I'm making change in my community for the better and that feeling is near indescribable.
I am over the moon right now - so happy with life.

You rock! It's awesome you took that leap and landed in something you obviously have passion for. Most people will live their lives always wondering "what if" on their passions and dreams. You are living something few have the fortitude to run with. I wish you all the best in your growth and success in your passion for cooking and living your passion.
